text:
STL carried the play for most of the night and still lost it 27 seconds into overtime, when Darnell Nurse beat Joel Hofer from a chance worth about 21 percent. The Blues out-chanced San Jose 3.76 to 2.96 in expected goals and took 56 shot attempts to 51, and in 63 percent of simulated replays of every shot they win. They got an early lead from Connor McMichael's tip-in and a shorthanded goal from Dillon Dube in the third, a 9 percent look that gave them a 2-1 edge they could not hold.

The Sharks survived because of Alex Nedeljkovic. Facing shots worth 3.76 expected goals, he allowed two in regulation and overtime, which put him 1.76 goals better than expected. St. Louis was at its sharpest in the first period, when it created 1.75 expected goals to San Jose's 0.4, yet it led only 1-0 after 20 minutes. The Sharks pulled even in the second on Tyler Toffoli's wrist shot, and the game turned in the third, when San Jose held the edge in chance quality, 1.03 to 0.41.

Collin Graf tied it at 2-2 at 6:05 of the third with a snap shot from Sam Dickinson and Toffoli, and Toffoli, the game's first star with a goal and an assist, was on the ice for 1.42 expected goals for against 0.84 against. Nurse then ended it, set up by Ivar Stenberg and Alexander Wennberg. Neither side scored on the power play, and St. Louis had the better of the game's shape but not its final shot. Hofer finished with essentially expected numbers (-0.04), so the gap came from the other crease.
